clips.title: The story
paras: Sting of the Scorpid is an early trial assigned by Gornek to Horde recruits at the Den in the Valley of Trials. Novices are challenged to hunt venomous scorpid workers northwest of camp and return ten tails to prove their combat readiness. The task serves as a vital lesson in surviving battlefield hazards and respecting even the smallest adversaries.

In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Gornek tests novice Horde recruits by sending them against the local wildlife. The venomous scorpids roaming the arid dirt northwest of the Den have humbled seasoned warriors and clumsy initiates alike. To prove their battlefield competence, young champions must venture into the rocks, slay scorpid workers, and return with ten of their severed tails as proof of prowess.

While deadly, the venomous predators also supply the very salvation of injured initiates. The Den maintains stockpiles of antivenom brewed directly from extracted scorpid venom to treat fallen novices. Beyond surviving the venom, Gornek emphasizes a core tactical truth: in the chaos of battle, arrogance is fatal, and even the smallest foe wields enough lethal venom to bring down a mighty warrior.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Powerful warrior and awkward novice alike have fallen to the venomous sting of the scorpid. You will find large numbers of scorpids northwest of here. Bring me ten of their tails as proof of your prowess in battle.
The antidote for their sting is actually made from venom extracted from their stingers. We keep large quantities of antidote for scorpid venom on hand to heal young bloods just like you...
But I'm sure you won't be needing any of that, will you?

clips.title: Progress
paras: The carapace of a scorpid isn't so thick that the strength of a determined warrior will be deterred. Strike strongly and without doubt, and the scorpids should prove easy prey.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There is an important lesson that you must take away from fighting scorpids. The smallest or largest of opponents can still send you to your doom. In fierce combat, any number of things can prove your downfall.
I have no more to teach you, friend. You have done well, and I will watch your progress with interest.
